title: Nether Beast Character Study: Blaming the Brood's bruises on the Hebrews (13_9)
summary: Part five of NH's exposé of YouTuber Nether Beast, covering fake 20-inch arm measurements, photoshopped thumbnails, the '20 years in the iron game' and muscle memory excuses, apparently bought subscribers, funneling viewers into sales, revisionism about his past exposure, and grandiose narcissism. NH draws lessons on how to measure properly and spot fitness frauds.
claims: Claims of 20-inch arms are a common fraud red flag; they're extremely hard to reach, especially natural and lean
A twisted or loose tape adds inches; NH estimates Nether added at least four inches in an interview clip
Measure arms with the tape tight all around, showing both sides and no slack
Regaining five inches of arm in a few months after losing about 40 lb of muscle is impossible
The neck holds size well naturally, but PED users lose neck size dramatically when off, as seen in MMA fighters
Real strength athletes have well-developed legs and posterior chains; chicken legs contradict world-record lifting claims
Hiding the body under shirts and camera angles after coming off drugs suggests body dysmorphia
Years of training mean nothing on their own; what matters is how long you've trained hard and consistently
Muscle memory speeds regaining lost muscle, perhaps cutting 10 years of work to five or six, but isn't magic
There is no evidence that training while starving stores up unrepaired damage that turns into gains once you eat
A 700-subscriber jump with no view spike suggests bought subscribers
The common YouTube fitness pattern: start genuine, build an audience, then sell supplements or programs; consider leaving when a creator starts selling, NH included
Anything that works eventually becomes conventional, so communities that reject all orthodox methods are left with what doesn't work
NH has never plugged his channel in other creators' comments
Blaming 'the system' for every failure while taking credit for every success is a seductive but pathetic mindset
NH diagnoses Blowhole with vulnerable narcissism and Nether with grandiose narcissism; both crave attention and love
